label: original/delimiter phase where at least half of the inputs so far are i/a/g/j/o
explanation: Sparse unit (about 1% of steps) that tracks how much of the input prefix is made of the letters i, a, g, j, o (i and a count most; lifts for prev2_tok are 6.7x for i and 5.6x for a). It fires in the original phase from t=2 and most strongly at the <DEL> step (39% of activation mass, 4.7x lift). The largest activations are at <DEL> in short sequences built almost entirely from i/a/g/o/j (e.g. a i a <DEL>). It is nearly silent in the copy phase after the first output, and at t=0 and t=1. The current input also matters: b, u, h, k raise it and repeated tokens lower it, but this effect is weak. The predicate (at least 2 such letters, making up at least half of the prefix, t <= L) captures about 61% of dev mass at only about 0.2 precision, so the unit looks like a distributed readout of the hidden state rather than a clean detector. Adding a current-token condition raises precision to about 0.39 but cuts recall.
